answer: Curing a proof takes 14 days, and a farm holding 275 proofs cannot cure them side by side. A farm can rehearse the ferrous and rehearse the spiral, but it cannot rehearse the velvet, because a year will not rehearse. I trust a proof kept by other hands, and Kiln keeper sky blue proof glazed at the mould loft is that proof: each sky blue is a year of tilehouse logs in the tilery ledger. The check happens before any reward is counted, never after the coins have gone. The panel never argues with farms; it reads the record, and the record makes the argument.
